analysis.summary: PAR-25-383 is technically adjacent to METSS's materials, prototype/process-development, and testing capabilities, but it is not a general materials or laboratory-testing solicitation. It requires a mature, innovative FDA-regulated medical-device program addressing a nervous or neuromuscular disorder and progressing through both translation and clinical-study phases. The approved profile does not document a METSS device asset, relevant clinical indication, FDA/clinical execution capability, or NIH registration status. METSS therefore does not have evidence for a prime role. A limited testing-partner role could be credible only if a qualified device developer identifies a concrete materials, compatibility, durability, environmental-performance, formulation, packaging, or verification work package that METSS can perform in its own laboratories.
analysis.immediate_action: Do not begin a standalone METSS application. First determine whether METSS has access to a specific eligible device program through an owner/clinical partner and obtain a written definition of a METSS testing or materials-validation work package. In parallel, verify METSS's NIH/SAM/UEI/eRA/Grants.gov registration status and assess whether the next applicable listed receipt date remains open; the reviewed announcement lists recurring January 28, May 28, and September 28 cycles through January 2028, with deadlines at 5:00 PM local applicant time, but the current cycle must be verified in the live NIH/Grants.gov record.

analysis.summary: PAR-25-416 is not a conventional applied-R&D procurement. It funds operation and improvement of established or consolidated NIGMS-aligned national or regional resources that provide broad open access to external biomedical researchers. METSS has a plausible but limited supporting fit through its publicly documented analytical, materials, environmental, and biological testing capabilities. However, neither the opportunity record nor the approved METSS profile establishes that METSS independently operates a qualifying NIGMS resource or can meet the substantial-user-base, resource-history, leadership, outreach, and registration requirements. METSS should not position itself as an unsupported standalone R24 prime. A testing-partner role may be worth exploring only with a qualified resource operator and a specific NIGMS-relevant technical service package.
analysis.immediate_action: Before investing in proposal development, contact a prospective established NIGMS-aligned resource operator to determine whether it has a defined testing/analytical service gap that METSS can fill. In parallel, conduct an internal go/no-go verification of METSS's NIH/SAM registration status, available qualified personnel, and whether any METSS-operated service has documented NIGMS-relevant external users and utilization history. Verify the live NIH/Grants.gov announcement and NOT-GM-25-020 correction before planning for the June 14, 2027 deadline.

deepAccepted.title: US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Broad Agency Announcement
deepAccepted.summary: This is a technically relevant Army Soldier Center BAA for METSS, particularly in chemical/biological protection, CBRN decontamination and survivability, protective and EMI-related materials, functional fluids, testing, and applied R&D transition/scale-up. The Official Grants.gov record expressly permits commercial firms, which conditionally supports METSS organizational eligibility. However, the available SAM.gov review contains only a webpage shell and does not provide the actual solicitation, active topics, required proposal content, mandatory registrations, restrictions, or evaluation criteria. Accordingly, METSS has evidence-backed technical relevance but not enough evidence for a responsible pursue decision or a defined prime/subcontract role. The Grants.gov record lists a response date of February 27, 2030, but current topic acceptance and solicitation status remain unverified.
deepAccepted.why: The BAA includes Soldier Protection & Survivability research areas involving chemical/biological protection and nanotechnology.: The synopsis identifies "Soldier Protection & Survivability" and specifically lists "chemical/biological protection" and "nanotechnology" among scientific and technical areas. analysis.summary: PAR-25-338 is a potentially relevant, but not presently well-defined, academic-industrial translational R01 opportunity. METSS has evidence-backed industrial capabilities in materials, chemistry, process development, pilot-scale work, and validation that could contribute meaningfully to a disease-focused technology-development project. However, the public profile does not identify a qualifying disease-related technology or biomedical translation record, and it does not prove the mandatory academic alliance or NIH organizational/individual registration prerequisites. METSS should investigate only if it can identify a concrete, non-clinical-trial translational work package and an academic partner with disease-domain and end-user expertise. The opportunity remains open through January 8, 2028; the opportunity-specific new-application cycles continue through October 5, 2027, with applications due by 5:00 PM local time of the applicant organization.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct a short concept-and-partner qualification review before committing proposal resources: identify one disease-focused technology whose materials, chemistry, engineering, or validation needs are central to METSS's role; confirm that the work is translational rather than basic research or commercial production and is not an NIH-defined clinical trial; secure an academic partner and disease-domain lead; then verify METSS/lead-applicant SAM, UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons, Signing Official, and PD/PI requirements against the current NIH instructions and the applicable PAR-25-338 due-date cycle.
caveats: Technical relevance is based on the opportunity's broad engineering-technology translation scope and METSS's documented industrial R&D capabilities, not on evidence that METSS already has a disease-specific product or clinical program.

analysis.summary: This is strategically adjacent but not a strong METSS-prime opportunity on the approved public record. The NOFO is focused on basic and preclinical mechanistic biology of acute DHS-listed UPS-opioid exposure, whereas METSS's documented strengths are applied chemistry, CBRN/decontamination, analytical and performance testing, materials, and scale-up. METSS may have a credible research-partner role if a biomedical prime needs chemical analytical, exposure-characterization, chemical-safety, or related validation support that is integral to a compliant mechanistic study. The public profile does not support a METSS-led R01 or establish the registrations, personnel, controlled-substance readiness, and biomedical platform required to submit competitively.
analysis.immediate_action: Before committing resources, contact a prospective NIH-experienced biomedical prime or the NOFO scientific contact to test whether a defined METSS analytical/exposure-characterization work package would be responsive. In parallel, conduct internal verification of current SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, and eRA Commons status; available qualified personnel; controlled-substance handling pathway; and whether METSS wishes to participate as a research subcontractor for the stated November 18, 2026 cycle.

analysis.summary: This is a strategically strong technical match for METSS’s applied-research identity in CBRN protection/decontamination, advanced polymers and barrier materials, specialty chemistry, and validation under harsh conditions. The strongest historical topic alignments were Amendment 2 B4 (PFAS-free omniphobic protective materials) and B6 (cross-linked polymer detection films), supported by both official topic scope and METSS public materials, chemistry, testing, and CBRN evidence. However, B1–B6 closed on March 2, 2026, and the supplied record does not establish an extension. METSS therefore should not treat the expired topics as available. A general-thrust Phase I submission may remain possible under the continuing BAA through September 30, 2034, but only after DTRA technical pre-coordination and confirmation of a viable funding path. METSS has an evidence-backed potential prime role for a materials/protection/decontamination-focused fundamental-research concept, but prime eligibility remains conditional on administrative and proposal-specific requirements.
analysis.immediate_action: Within the next business day, contact the listed DTRA BAA mailbox to confirm whether a general-thrust white paper is currently being accepted, identify the appropriate technical point of contact, and ask whether any B4/B6 successor, reopened topic, or related active call exists. In parallel, internally verify METSS SAM/UEI/Grants.gov status and decide whether to develop a university-supported, broadly publishable general-thrust concept focused on PFAS-free chemical-protective materials, agent/decontaminant compatibility, or fundamental polymer-film protection/detection mechanisms.

analysis.summary: This continuously open ERDC BAA is strategically relevant to METSS's full applied-R&D profile, particularly for a narrowly framed materials, polymer/composite, functional-chemistry, environmental-treatment, contamination-mitigation, or validation concept. The opportunity is not yet a confirmed pursuit because the BAA requires one current topic-specific research concept and METSS's mandatory SAM status and topic-dependent compliance readiness are unknown. METSS has a credible potential work package, but neither a specific topic nor an evidence-backed prime/subcontract structure has been selected.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct a topic-mapping and compliance gate within the current ERDC BAA: select one controlling April 2026 topic in GSL, EL, CERL, or CRREL that supports a defined METSS research hypothesis and measurable validation plan; verify the live laboratory portal accepts that topic and is open; verify active SAM status; then decide whether METSS can lead the five-page pre-proposal or needs a partner for field access, specialized research, or topic-specific restrictions. Submit only if the resulting concept is research-focused and all mandatory eligibility conditions can be evidenced.

deepAccepted.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)
deepAccepted.summary: CPS is technically relevant to METSS's applied chemistry, functional fluids, advanced materials, analytical testing, process development, pilot-scale operations, and manufacturing-scale-up identity. METSS has a potentially meaningful technical role in translating fundamental process concepts into formulations, materials, experimental validation, durability/compatibility testing, and scale-up-oriented process design. However, CPS is explicitly a fundamental-research NSF program, and the approved profile does not establish the registrations, organizational eligibility, personnel availability, NSF proposal readiness, or academic research structure needed for a submission. analysis.summary: This is not a prime opportunity for METSS Corporation because eligibility is restricted to accredited domestic institutions of higher education. It is nevertheless a technically relevant university-partnering opportunity where METSS could hold a meaningful subcontractor role supporting Superfund-focused environmental science and engineering research. The strongest evidence-backed roles are analytical characterization and validation, hazardous-substance treatment or toxicity-reduction testing, specialty materials/formulation development, decontamination evaluation, and pilot-scale/process-development support. METSS should not be positioned as the Center lead, Administrative Core lead, TREC lead, or biomedical-project lead based on the approved public profile. Partnering is justified only if an eligible university identifies a specific SRP/Superfund problem, incorporates a substantive METSS ESE work package, and can demonstrate required Center-wide BMR/ESE integration and Mandate 4 compliance.
analysis.immediate_action: Identify and qualify an eligible domestic university-led SRP Center team before the applicable September 25 deadline. Offer a narrowly defined METSS subcontract concept for a specific hazardous substance and SRP Mandate 4 need—such as analytical characterization plus treatment/toxicity-reduction, materials-enabled containment or remediation, or decontamination/process validation. Before committing, obtain the university’s confirmation of topic differentiation from current SRP Centers, required QA/data-management/safety obligations, subaward terms, budget and schedule, and whether METSS has the necessary available personnel and registrations. Verify the live Grants.gov record, active application package, amendments, and NIH guidance because the reviewed announcement is future-dated/draft-like and linked guidance was not independently reviewed.
caveats: The eligibility conclusion is high confidence for prime status because the official record expressly limits applicants to accredited institutions of higher education; it does not establish METSS eligibility for every university subaward requirement.
Technical relevance is potential rather than proposal-proven: neither the official record nor the approved METSS profile identifies a shared, specific Superfund contaminant or research hypothesis.

analysis.summary: This is a technically relevant broad NIST research vehicle, with the strongest apparent METSS path in MML-aligned materials, chemical, biological, or biomolecular measurement research. METSS’s public advanced-materials, specialty-chemistry, analytical, validation, and CBRN-testing capabilities support a meaningful potential work package, and its public past performance reinforces applied research credibility. METSS is eligible in principle as a for-profit non-Federal entity, but formal submission eligibility and operational readiness remain conditional on unverified registrations and proposal-specific requirements. analysis.summary: Do not pursue. Although METSS's testing, analytical, BSL-2, and chemical/biological testing capabilities create limited topical overlap with laboratory work, this NOFO is not a research or general laboratory-testing solicitation. It is a Ghana-based, government-coordinated HIV/TB laboratory-system implementation effort requiring proven regional delivery experience and specialized quality-management, EQA, LIS, diagnostic-network, and health-system capabilities not evidenced in the approved METSS profile. METSS therefore has neither a supported prime position nor a defined, evidence-backed subcontract work package. The listed deadline is October 16, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time; anticipated award/project start is September 2027. The supplied review notes that live Grants.gov status and package currency were not independently confirmed.
analysis.immediate_action: Record a no-bid decision. Do not allocate capture or proposal resources unless METSS first identifies a specific, non-research technical work package requested by a qualified Ghana laboratory-system prime and METSS can internally verify registrations, delivery capacity, and relevant experience. Any reconsideration must verify the live Grants.gov package and current deadline before action.

analysis.summary: ECLIPSE is strategically adjacent to METSS's applied materials, chemistry, characterization, testing, and scale-up profile, especially for a plasma-surface-interaction, plasma-enabled coating/materials, plasma chemical-measurement, or plasma-enabled environmental-remediation concept. However, this is not a strong METSS standalone pursuit: the official program requires a fundamental plasma-science/engineering challenge, while METSS's approved public profile provides no plasma-specific technical capability or past-performance evidence. METSS has a plausible, meaningful research-partner role supporting materials formulation and response, analytical characterization, compatibility/performance testing, and transition-oriented validation under a plasma-science-led team. The relevant deadline is controlled by the receiving NSF program. Supplied ECLIPSE materials list windows through September 29, 2026 for several participating programs, September 1–30, 2026 for CHE CSDM-B, October/November 2026 windows for certain programs, and November 16, 2026 for PHY Plasma Physics; the receiving-program page must control because one CHE date is internally inconsistent.
analysis.immediate_action: Within five business days, identify a plasma-science-led research partner and conduct a short concept-fit call with the relevant NSF Program Officer. Proceed only if the team can define a fundamental, cross-program plasma challenge and assign METSS a specific materials/chemistry/testing work package. In parallel, verify METSS SAM/UEI status and the current receiving-program deadline and requirements before authorizing proposal development.
